the neural mechanisms that enable weakly electric fish to sense the world around them.

temporal selectivity in the torus semicularis is an emergent property of both the temporal dynamics of active sensing and the intrinsic temporal dynamics of the neural circuits that process the sensory input.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
temporal selectivity in mid-brain electrosensory circuits is related to the dynamic temporal pattern of active sensing.

temporal selectivity of toral neurons may contribute to the ability of the fish to distinguish the temporal pattern of their own behavior and to discriminate among different behavioral contexts.
